To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SRTM elevation model is a suitable data source for delineating process-based model entities in different landscapes.

(1) SRTM data are suitable for delineation of model entities on an appropriate spatial resolution, (2) the delineated model entities are suitable to estimate the water balance, and (3) the delineated SRTM-based entities are applicable for modelling of hydrological processes.
SRTM data are useful to delineate topographic entities for hydrological modelling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method for the delineation of model entities for distributed hydrological models based on the topography.
the delineation of RUs for hydrological modelling in ungauged catchments using SRTM data.
the delineation of topographic entities using SRTM data and their integration in hydrological modelling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method of delineation of process-oriented model units is feasible and that the method can be applied to different landscapes and different scales of analysis.
the method of the extraction of process-based topography model units is applicable for the application of distributed hydrological models.
the SRTM-based extraction of model entities is feasible and can be used for the estimation of the water balance in ungauged catchments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the delineation of model entities is possible using SRTM data, and that the entities represent a valid basis for hydrological modelling in ungauged and poorly gauged basins.
the delineation of RUs is a suitable method for the estimation of runoff dynamics in ungauged areas.
the integration of landscape parameters is possible and feasible for ungauged catchments.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the delineation of RUs using SRTM data is a promising approach for the application in ungauged areas.
SRTM-based entities are able to represent the spatial heterogeneity of the landscape in a way that the runoff generation can be estimated using a process-based model.
the delineation of RUs can be used for the development of a new approach to the estimation of the runoff coefficient in ungauged catchments.
